palette.notes: Not pixel art: a hand-painted oil/acrylic portrait where a band across the eyes is painted as large flat squares of skin tones. Measured palette_size 0 (the frame is not a clean palette). The squares are oranges, peaches and browns sampled from the painting.

lighting: Natural studio light on a physical canvas; within the painting, warm skin with red nose and cool blue eyes.
silhouette: Not relevant; the hook is the grid of big squares over a realistic face.

motion.timing: Measured 12.54 drawings/s, median hold 33.3 ms: live camera and the hand moving the brush, not animation. The painter fills one square at a time over 20 s.

texture: Thick painted brush texture on the realistic face vs. flat even squares in the pixel band; a pencilled grid still visible.
camera: Static close-up of the canvas, hand and brush entering from the right.

acting.enters: The brush and hand come in from the right side of frame.
acting.acts: Paints squares in the band one by one; the joke is a realistic portrait being 'pixelated' by hand.

techniques: not pixel art: a painting with a hand-painted pixelation band, noted for the style-clash hook
realistic image + blocky censor-bar squares = instant visual contrast
process video: one square per stroke, progress visible frame to frame
feel: realistic painted face + hand-painted pixel bar = 'wait, what?' style clash (painting, not pixel art)
for_fred: Try a style-clash beat: show something realistic (Robert's footage) with a small area turned into big pixel blocks where Fred pokes through, so the pixel world breaks into the real one.
